summary: Single-author interpretive synthesis arguing software engineering is shifting from code authorship toward orchestration, verification and governance of AI agents. It proposes three coexisting paradigms (Traditional, GenAI-enabled, Agentic), a five-category competency framework with a matrix, and nine untested propositions, grounded mainly in a curated core corpus of 12 sources (Table 1), chiefly the AIDev PR dataset.

claims.claim: Agentic contribution is large-scale but trust lags: agent PRs are merged less often, especially for complex tasks.
claims.evidence: §4.2 restates AIDev findings (456,535 PRs) from a single cited source [1]; no new analysis.

claims.claim: Effort is migrating to specification, verification, integration and governance.
claims.evidence: §4.3 cites four sources (Acharya, Sun & Staron, Betz & Penzenstadler, Kohl & Carro) mostly position papers; no quantitative measure of effort.

claims.claim: An original competency framework (FSE-CF) with five categories organizes future engineer capabilities.
claims.evidence: §8 framework derived by author coding; no expert validation, Delphi, or empirical test.

claims.claim: Nine falsifiable propositions (e.g., throughput gated by verification capacity).
claims.evidence: Table 8 lists propositions and suggested tests; none tested.

patterns.note: Argues intent specification becomes the engineer's core value; no evidence on spec-driven tooling.
Accountable human oversight emphasized; proposition P8 for safety-critical domains, untested.
Notes provider-aligned agent/review-bot 'closed loops' risk (from AIDev), proposition P4.

methodology.sample: Core corpus of 12 sources (Table 1) plus foundational references; no search string, databases, or PRISMA-style counts.

biases.detail: Synthesis rests on a curated 12-source core corpus with no reproducible search protocol.
Curated inclusion by a single author; §10 concedes alternative syntheses are possible and corpus skews to open source.
Paradigm shift / competency framing restates widely held positions from the cited roadmaps.
Framework and propositions are not validated by experts or data.

coi.affiliations: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA), Riyadh — government body.

verdict_reason: Position-style synthesis with a 12-source hand-curated corpus, no search protocol, single author coding, and no empirical validation of the framework or propositions; it adds no harness-decision evidence beyond what the cited AIDev study already provides.
applicability: Does not inform a concrete harness decision for the Java ingestion team. At most it is background framing for why spec-driven development (intent specification + verification) and human oversight gates matter in a regulated healthcare-education context; the team should cite primary empirical sources (e.g., AIDev) instead. Nothing here addresses multi-repo ingestion, mixed agent hosts, or Java.
